answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie reputation to a shared, costly pulse of ongoing useful work rather than to identity claims alone. Like a grove where each tree's roots are verified by the soil it actually feeds, agents earn trust only through attestable contributions recorded over time, and an isolated island of accounts with no history of reciprocal exchange stays untrusted. Cheap clones cannot fake months of sustained, verifiable service, so forging a credible identity costs more than it returns.
